title: Dots Above — the measured mark
concept: The canonical wordmark: three word-bounded dots (Ø468 = 0.64·cap, gap 132) resting on the optical centres of H·R·L.
why: The exact baseline mark the typography study converged on — instantly Julia-family, perfectly balanced above the caps.
risk: Front-loaded: the beats' centroid sits ~497 left of the word centre; prefer left-aligned lockups.
anim: Each dot is a bounce-landing point; the three fade in H→R→L as the ball stamps them.
prints: Reads in 1 colour if the dots become ink outlines.
color: H purple · R red · L green; the only three-colour element.

title: Comb Below — 12 ticks of time, 3 beats
concept: The hero idea: a comb of 12 equal ticks (one per letter = equal time) runs under the word; three beats rest on it at cells 0·5·9 — the letters H·R·L, an inter-beat pattern of 5:4.
why: The name becomes a recording: regular time grid + irregular beats = HRV, encoded in the monospace itself.
risk: The comb adds height; a header/hero mark, not a square favicon.
anim: The three balls bounce along the comb floor and colour H·R·L on contact; the 12 ticks are the metronome.
prints: Excellent 1-colour: ticks + word ink, beats filled or outlined.
color: Beats H purple · R red · L green on a neutral grey comb.
top3_reason: Your comb-at-bottom concept, made exact: 12 equal ticks are time, the three beats land on H·R·L at a real 5:4 interval, so the wordmark *is* an HRV trace. Purpose-built for the bounce.

title: Full System — dots above + comb below
concept: Both registers: beats float above the caps AND a faint time-comb underlines the word with three colour-matched beat-ticks under H·R·L.
why: The most complete statement — beats, letters and time grid in one balanced stack.
risk: Busiest of the set; keep the comb faint so the dots lead.
anim: Two-phase: ball bounces along the comb, then stamped beats rise to rest above the caps.
prints: The faint comb drops cleanly in 1-colour; dots carry the colour.
color: Three hues twice; keep comb ticks grey to avoid four-colour noise.

title: Comb Underline — the signature
concept: Series-2's favourite, re-fitted: the whole wordmark is underlined by the equal comb; the three ticks under H·R·L are dot-capped in colour, inline with the type.
why: Reads as a data-signature rather than decoration, and now the tick spacing is the true monospace grid.
risk: At small sizes the underline can merge into a solid rule; fall back to an icon for favicons.
anim: The dot-caps are the deposited beats: they pop in on the bounce while the grey ticks stay static as the time axis.
prints: One-colour friendly: whole comb + word ink, only the three caps tinted.
color: Only the three beat-caps carry colour — a restrained, editorial palette use.
top3_reason: My overall pick. It fuses both things you liked into one metric-exact mark — the wordmark riding its own inter-beat comb — and is the most animation-ready: grey ticks hold as the time axis while the three colour caps stamp in on the bounce. Best for README/docs headers.

title: Bounce Still — ball in flight
concept: A frozen frame of the motion spec: purple beat already stamped on H; the ball (now red, about to stamp R) at the apex of the H→R arc with float-stretch and a smear ghost; comb floor beneath.
why: Sells the animation in one static image — the mark is alive and rule-driven (apex ∝ distance²).
risk: A motion still, not a resting logo; use for animated contexts.
anim: This IS the key-frame; arc, squash and colour hand-off are all in GUIDELINES §7.
prints: Motion stills rarely print; use word-dots-above as the print fallback.
color: Ball colour = the colour it is about to stamp (red for R); trailing ghost at lower opacity.

title: Orange Middle — the open question
concept: The comb-below mark with the middle beat in a literal orange (#E8802B) instead of Julia red — the alternative the guidelines left open.
why: Warmer, higher-contrast triad (purple·orange·green); resolves the open colour question for direct comparison.
risk: Orange isn't an official Julia hex; reads slightly less 'Julia-family'.
anim: Same bounce; only the R stamp colour changes — one variable to A/B (RD→ORG).
prints: Orange prints more vividly than the muted red on coated stock.
color: Purple · orange · green — one-place change if adopted (middle beat only).

title: Monochrome — 1-colour / print
concept: A single-ink cut: all letters ink, the three beats as ink outline-rings above the caps so the triad survives with no colour.
why: Guarantees one-colour use — engraving, embossing, stamps, dark-mode knockout.
risk: Loses the Julia colour identity; pair with a colour version where colour exists.
anim: Rings can animate by stroke-dashoffset (draw-on) instead of fill — a different elegant motion.
prints: Purpose-built for print: 1 ink, thick strokes, no fine ticks; knocks out to white on dark.
color: Zero colour; the three-dot rhythm carries identity through form alone.

title: HRL — dots above
concept: The compact monogram: three tinted capitals H·R·L with three beats resting above their optical centres.
why: The smallest mark still carrying the three-letter / three-beat / three-colour story; a natural app icon.
risk: Three equal letters lose the 5:4 variability story; this is identity, not data.
anim: Same bounce over three (equal) hops; colours stamp H→R→L.
color: H purple · R red · L green.

title: HRL — comb below
concept: HRL over a three-tick comb (one tick per letter, equal width = time); three beats rest on the ticks.
why: The comb-at-bottom idea in favicon form; balls bounce on three ticks and colour each letter.
risk: With only three equal ticks the time grid reads more decorative than data.
anim: The perfect tiny bounce loop: three ticks, three landings, three colour stamps.
color: Beats and caps share the three hues.
top3_reason: The compact companion to the wordmark and the cleanest home for the bounce loop you described: three balls drop onto three time-ticks and light up H·R·L in turn. Crops to a favicon and is the obvious thing to animate.

title: HRL Ring — the round logo
concept: The round version: HRL centred inside a ring of 12 equal ticks (time folded into a circle); three beats sit at the angles for cells 0·5·9 — the 5:4 pattern, wrapped.
why: A distinct circular emblem that still encodes the exact rhythm; the natural seal / avatar form.
risk: Ticks are small on the ring; keep above ~48px or use the clean ring.
anim: KEY animation: the ring unrolls into the straight comb and the beats slide to H·R·L — a round intro that resolves into the wordmark.
prints: Round marks centre well on pins/coins/stickers; strong square crop.
color: Three beats on a grey ring, HRL tinted in the centre.

title: HRL Ring — clean (favicon-round)
concept: The ring stripped to essentials: HRL centred, three evenly-spaced beats on a plain ring, no minor ticks.
why: The most favicon-proof round mark — reads at 16px where the ticked ring would mush.
risk: Even 120° spacing drops the 5:4 story for legibility; the folded, tidied logo.
anim: Beats orbit the ring, then it opens into the line for the wordmark reveal.
prints: Cleanest round mark for tiny/print use.
color: Three hues on a neutral ring.

title: HRL — favicon
concept: Ultra-compact: HRL with three small beats above, sized for 16–32px.
why: The smallest legible carrier of the identity; what actually ships as the favicon.
risk: No comb/time story — pure identity at tiny size.
anim: Too small to animate meaningfully; static.

title: Unroll Still — ring → line
concept: A mid-transition frame: the ring has partly opened into an arc, three beats strung along it approaching their H·R·L positions — the concept key-frame for the round→linear reveal.
why: Documents the signature animation move for later production; also a lively in-motion badge.
risk: Transitional by nature — not a resting logo.
anim: The storyboard frame for the round-intro → wordmark animation.
color: Beats keep their hues through the unroll.

title: Stacked — HRL emblem over wordmark
concept: A two-tier lockup: the compact HRL-triad monogram (dots above three tinted caps) floats centred above the full 'HeartRateLab' wordmark.
why: Gives a real vertical brand lockup (icon over name) for square cards, splash screens and app stores — distinct from the flat dots-above mark.
risk: Two focal tiers need vertical breathing room; not for short banners.
anim: The monogram can animate first (its own mini-bounce), then the wordmark rises in beneath it.
color: Three hues in the monogram; the wordmark caps repeat them.

title: Caliper — the 5:4, measured
concept: The wordmark with two dimension calipers under it spanning H→R (3008) and R→L (2416) — measuring the two inter-beat intervals and showing the 5:4 ratio.
why: The most explicit 'this measures intervals' lockup; a teaching mark for docs and papers.
risk: More diagram than logo; best where the story can breathe.
anim: Calipers draw on after the beats land, annotating the rhythm — a great explanatory animation.
prints: Fine linework; keep ≥200px or thicken for print.

title: Ticks Rising — beats grow from the comb
concept: Series-2's 'ticks rising' idea, fixed to the grid: 12 equal grey ticks under the word; the three under H·R·L grow tall and terminate in coloured beats.
why: Ties each beat to its exact time-tick, so the marks read as events on the axis, not free-floating dots.
risk: The tall coloured ticks can look like stems; keep beat radius clearly larger than tick width.
anim: The three ticks extend upward on the beat, launching the balls — a growth-into-bounce transition.

title: Minimal Underline — three ticks only
concept: The most restrained lockup: a thin baseline under the word with just three coloured ticks at H·R·L, the rest of the comb implied.
why: The quietest way to carry the beat identity horizontally — great for dense UI and README badges.
risk: Without the full comb it reads as three marks, not a grid; the data story is implicit.
anim: The three ticks blink in on the bounce; minimal motion, maximal restraint.
prints: Superb 1-colour and tiny-size behaviour (three short strokes).
color: Only three tinted ticks — the leanest palette use in the set.

title: Round Badge — emblem + wordmark
concept: A lockup pairing the clean beat-ring emblem (left) with the 'HeartRateLab' wordmark (right).
why: A formal emblem-plus-name lockup for headers, papers and about-pages; the round mark also stands alone.
risk: Two focal shapes need careful spacing; provided at the measured alignment.
anim: The ring spins/unrolls on load, then the wordmark fades in beside it.
color: Ring beats + word caps share the three hues.
